## My Reasoning

I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it, and I know this soil. I have about 8 mu of contracted land. Every year I grow winter wheat, then summer maize on the same ground. That is what everyone here does. That is what works.

I am 66 now. My back is not what it was. My son lives in Shijiazhuang and cannot help much during planting. So I keep things simple — the same rotation I have done for 30 years. I hire a machine for rotary tilling before wheat and for harvest. That saves my body.

For wheat, I will use an improved variety — Jimai 22, what the seed shop in town sells most. For maize, I always buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid. I have used it for many years and yields are good. I do not experiment with new varieties I have not seen. Too risky at my age.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer as a base, then urea as topdressing at jointing. My neighbor uses about 15 jin of urea per mu at topdressing, so I do the same. I know I should probably use less water — the government has been saying so — but wheat needs water at jointing and heading or the grain shrivels. I will irrigate three times for wheat. Maize gets rain in summer mostly, maybe one irrigation if July is dry.

I spray herbicide on the wheat in winter, and spray once more in spring for aphids and powdery mildew if I see it. For maize I spray once for corn borer. I do not like handling pesticides much anymore but you cannot skip it.
